message.abstract:
<jats:title>Significance</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The vast majority of evidence marshaled for the Late Heavy Bombardment comes from
                    <jats:sup>40</jats:sup>
                    Ar/
                    <jats:sup>39</jats:sup>
                    Ar age spectra of Apollo samples, interpreted through “plateau” ages, which show an apparent cluster at ∼3.9 Ga. Whether such data can be uniquely inverted to constrain impact histories in the Earth−Moon system has never been tested. We show that diffusive loss of
                    <jats:sup>40</jats:sup>
                    Ar from a monotonically declining impactor flux coupled with the early and episodic nature of lunar crust formation tends to create clustered distributions of apparent
                    <jats:sup>40</jats:sup>
                    Ar/
                    <jats:sup>39</jats:sup>
                    Ar ages at
                    <jats:italic>ca.</jats:italic>
                    3.9 Ga. Instead, these
                    <jats:sup>40</jats:sup>
                    Ar/
                    <jats:sup>39</jats:sup>
                    Ar data can be reconciled with a continuously decreasing bollide flux. Thus, impacts may have played a minimal role in terrestrial habitability, early Earth dynamics, and the formation of Hadean zircons.
                  </jats:p>
title: Illusory Late Heavy Bombardments
